function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you pull the node data you’re after, but I’ll need a bit more detail to make the right API call.

The function we have available (`telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get`) requires the following parameters:

| Parameter | What it represents | Example |
|-----------|--------------------|---------|
| `fabricName` | Name of the fabric you’re querying (e.g., `"test-de"`). | `"test-de"` |
| `nodeId` | Numeric ID of the node you want data for. | `101` |
| `podId` | Numeric ID of the pod that contains the node. | `1` |
| `interfaceType` | Type of interface you’re interested in (`"svi"`, `"ethernet"`, `"loopback"`, or `"port-channel"`). | `"ethernet"` |
| `infoType` | Kind of information you want (`"interfaces"`, `"status"`, `"statistics"`, or `"errors"`). | `"status"` |

Since you mentioned the IP address `23.31.32.1`, I’m guessing you want to look up the node that has that IP. Unfortunately, the function expects a numeric `nodeId`, not an IP address. If you already know the node’s numeric ID (or can look it up via another API), you can plug it in along with the other details.

**Example call (replace the placeholders with your actual values):**

```python
response = functions.telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get({
    "fabricName": "test-de",
    "nodeId": 123,          # <-- replace with the node’s numeric ID
    "podId": 1,             # <-- replace with the pod’s numeric ID
    "interfaceType": "ethernet",
    "infoType": "status"
})
print(response)
```

If you don’t yet know the node’s numeric ID, you’ll need to query the fabric’s inventory first (via a separate endpoint or CLI command) to map the IP `23.31.32.1` to its node ID and pod ID. Once you have those, you can use the snippet above.

Let me know if you’d like help figuring out the node ID from the IP, or if you have the node/pod IDs ready and want to proceed with the call!
